title: Preparing for Employment Costs S. Koreans $440 a Month
paragraphs: Looking for a job can be expensive in South Korea. According to a new survey, young job seekers spend an average of about 580,000 won, or roughly $440, every month to prepare for employment.

The survey was carried out for the Federation of Korean Industries, a large business group. It asked 1,000 people between the ages of 19 and 34 who are currently looking for work about their spending over the past three months.

The biggest cost was fees for qualification and language tests, which made up 30.7% of spending. Education costs came second at 22.6%, followed by textbooks and study materials at 16.1%. Transportation made up 12.4%, and 7.3% was spent on places to study, such as cafes and study cafes.

The amount people spent depended on several things. Those who wanted to work for large companies spent about 700,000 won a month, while those aiming for smaller companies spent less. People who had been looking for a job for more than three years spent about 800,000 won a month.
Most young people said the costs were hard to manage. Around 69.3% said they felt a financial burden, while only 7.3% said they did not.
The money came from different places. About 32.8% came from parents and family, 29.5% from part-time work or other income, and 27.3% from personal savings. Only 7.9% came from government support.
When asked what kind of help they wanted most, 25.9% chose support for test fees. Others wanted help with rent or general job-search vouchers.

Lee Sang-ho, a director at the Federation of Korean Industries, said many young job seekers feel a heavy financial burden. He called for more support with test fees and education costs, especially for young people from low-income families.
